country.comment: Study examines three municipalities (Comitán de Domínguez, La Trinitaria, and La Independencia) in the Río Grande de Comitán-Lagos de Montebello watershed in Chiapas, Mexico.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title and Abstract; PDF p. 4, Section Study area

effect_estimate.comment: Descriptive spatial, administrative, and non-parametric trend analyses are reported without inferential regression effect sizes, confidence intervals, or p-values linking institutional variables to water or health outcomes.
effect_estimate.value: Descriptive municipal comparisons only (no inferential regression coefficients, CIs, or p-values reported): Across 1994–2019 REPDA water-rights permits in the RGCLM watershed, agricultural uses held 1,083 concessions versus 192 concessions for municipal/domestic public use, taking 93% of groundwater permits (588 vs. 36 domestic) and 70% of surface-water permits (344 vs. 149 domestic). Under CONAGUA's centralized scheme prioritizing urban settlements >2,500 inhabitants, urban-dominated Comitán de Domínguez received 90% of domestic public water volume (~18 hm³ for 166,178 inhabitants) and possessed the sole urban sewerage/wastewater plant, whereas more marginalized rural municipalities received 8% in La Trinitaria (83,111 inhabitants) and 2% in La Independencia (46,409 inhabitants) (~2 hm³ jointly) while accounting for 46% and 42% of agricultural water volume (~18 hm³ jointly). Indeterminate gastrointestinal morbidity and cancer mortality (3,074 of 5,006 potentially toxic-related deaths in 1998–2019) showed increasing trends alongside rising income inequality (Palma ratio, 2000–2010) and persistent rural marginalization (2015–2020).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF pp. 7–9, Section Results; PDF p. 9, Section Discussion (Individual and collective action)

mechanism_certainty.comment: Rated 1 (documented association) within the cross-sectional/ecological design ceiling (max 2): the study documents municipal-level descriptive disparities in formal REPDA water-rights concessions alongside marginalization and waterborne/toxic health trends across three municipalities, while discussing CONAGUA's >2,500-inhabitant urban priority rule, weak pesticide regulation/enforcement, and informal community arrangements without directly observing administrative permitting or enforcement processes operating at the household level.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 5–6, Section Methods; PDF pp. 7–8, Section Results; PDF pp. 9–11, Section Discussion and Conclusion

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines formal CONAGUA water-rights permits/concessions (property) under a centralized scheme prioritizing urban settlements >2,500 inhabitants (service_area), urban/spatial and watershed land-use planning (planning), community collective action and participatory urbanization (participation), uncoordinated sectoral SDG governance across levels (institutional_fragmentation), and weak agrochemical/water-quality regulation and enforcement (ENFORCEMENT).

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Ecological observational case study of three municipalities using aggregated secondary spatial, administrative permit, census, and morbidity/mortality datasets with descriptive mapping and non-parametric trend smoothing, and no individual longitudinal cohort follow-up or quasi-experimental intervention comparator.
risk_of_bias_tool.value: JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies

sample_size.comment: Primary spatial unit of analysis is 3 municipalities encompassing 295,698 inhabitants across an 81,000-ha watershed (note PDF p. 4 contains a typographic omission stating '295 persons', whereas PDF p. 7 reports the exact municipal inhabitant counts summing to 295,698). Secondary datasets analyzed across these 3 municipalities cover REPDA water concessions (1994–2019), INEGI land-cover maps (2002, 2007, 2017), morbidity surveillance (1998–2018), mortality records (1998–2019), and census/marginalization indices (2000, 2010, 2015, 2020).
sample_size.value: 3 municipalities in the RGCLM watershed (Comitán de Domínguez: 166,178 inhabitants; La Trinitaria: 83,111 inhabitants; La Independencia: 46,409 inhabitants; total 295,698 inhabitants across 81,000 ha); secondary administrative records analyzed include 634 groundwater (49%) and 495 surface-water (38%) REPDA concessions (1,083 agricultural and 192 domestic/municipal concessions, 1994–2019), 3 INEGI land-cover map series (2002, 2007, 2017), weekly municipal morbidity records for 36 disease types (1998–2018), and 5,006 municipal deaths potentially associated with toxic compounds/pesticides (1998–2019)

study_design.comment: Secondary quantitative/spatial ecological case study across three municipalities; although Discussion p. 9 briefly alludes to prior field observations citing Alvarado Velázquez et al. (2022), the Methods and Results contain exclusively secondary spatial, registry, epidemiological, and census analyses.
study_design.value: Ecological observational case study of three municipalities using secondary spatial and administrative data (GIS land-cover change analysis for 2002–2017, spatial/descriptive analysis of REPDA water-rights concessions for 1994–2019, non-parametric local polynomial regression of municipal morbidity and mortality trends for 1998–2019, and descriptive municipal inequality/marginalization comparisons for 2000–2020)
study_design.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF pp. 4–6, Section Methods

evidence_quotes.quote: Drawing on the case study of three municipalities in the Río Grande de Comitán-Lagos de Montebello watershed in Chiapas, Mexico, we illustrate some of the consequences of the intensification of agricultural activities, alongside urban expansion, at the expense of forests and the negative impact on the water quality of surrounding areas during the last two decades.

By type of use, agricultural activities comprise the main users (1083 concessions) in the RGCLM watershed, followed by concessions for municipal and domestic public use (192 concessions). The majority of the concessions for agricultural use are localized in La Independencia and La Trinitaria. Groundwater sources (588 concessions, 93%) were largely for agricultural activities, while only 6% (36 concessions) were for domestic public use.

evidence_quotes.criterion: sample_size and effect_estimate (domestic water volume disparity)
evidence_quotes.quote: In terms of water for domestic public use, Comitán de Domínguez was, by far, the main user (90% of the volume, for 166,178 inhabitants), followed by La Trinitaria (8% of the volume, for 83,111 inhabitants) and La Independencia (2% of the volume, for 46,409 inhabitants).

evidence_quotes.criterion: mechanism_flags (water concessions and urban population threshold)
evidence_quotes.page: PDF Page 9, Discussion, Section Individual and collective action
evidence_quotes.quote: Water concessions in Mexico are granted by the federal authority, the National Water Commission (Comisión Nacional del Agua [CONAGUA]), under a centralized scheme that prioritizes water access to urban areas larger than 2500 inhabitants.

evidence_quotes.page: PDF Page 9, Discussion, Section Individual and collective action
evidence_quotes.quote: These are examples of how collective action has filled the gap caused by the lack of government management mechanisms to resolve the provisioning of water.

The intensification of agricultural activities in the RGCLM watershed is coupled with poor regulation and enforcement, allowing the use of persistent pesticides with potential effects on human health.
